title: I got laid off, so I built Dunya Arena: a Footman Frenzy-inspired Arena RTS
author: SoberSonderr
selftext:
Back before my friends and I could afford a Ventrilo server (or even knew how servers worked), we’d get on a three-way phone call, patch each other in, tie up the phone line, and play Footman Frenzy, the Warcraft 3 custom map, for hours.

I’ve had design notes for a standalone game inspired by it since 2016, but never got past the idea. I was laid off in April, and instead of jumping straight back into the job hunt, I decided to finally build it.

Dunya Arena is an Arena RTS where your halls build troops automatically. There are no workers and no build orders: you lead a hero, decide where your army fights, and choose what it becomes. Think a mix of Footman Frenzy, Total War: Arena and Dota/League of Legends.  
How it plays:

Your halls build your army. Each hall spawns troops automatically, and you can rally them and arrange them in formations. You upgrade your halls through four tiers, commit to a faction, and buy attack and defense upgrades for your army.

You play one hero from a roster of 20, with concepts for 50. Each hero has their own kit that you level up during the match, plus items to shape your playstyle.

The center is the objective. Both teams fight for the Favor of the Gods, which boosts mana regen and income. The game ends when all enemy halls are destroyed.

I’m one person with no art budget, so AI tools are what made this possible. I already have a pretty extensive dev and IT background, so leveraging AI for assets helped a ton. That being said, AI-assisted coding did really help with development timeframes and I do eventually want to replace AI art with custom, human made models. The buildings, units, terrain, music, sounds are all licensed and human made. 

The world and its lore come from a tabletop campaign I’ve been running for 10+ years. It started in D&D, moved to Pathfinder, and we still play most Mondays.

I’m looking for play testers. I need people who’ll play it, break it, complain about it and tell me what feels off. I host playtests every week or two on Discord. Comment or DM me for a beta key.

A free demo is coming in January of next year with the release shortly after.

For other devs here: how are you handling AI-generated art versus code in your own projects? And if you ever played Footman Frenzy, what do you remember most from it?

[Steam page, if you want to wishlist and follow along](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5027980/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=announce&utm_content=r_aigamedev)

comments.author: behemensch
comments.body: Love the heroes and the world, such cool concepts. The gameplay has great swings where every decision matters whether it's items, skill builds, or positioning. I also enjoy the variety when it comes to roles, none of them are truly one-dimensional.

replies.author: SoberSonderr
replies.body: Thanks! A lot of time was spent on making sure every hero plays uniquely. Giving each hero its own identity is a very important design philosophy to me.

comments.author: CyberPope
comments.body: The second coming of Footman Frenzy in the best way, a solid modern take.  Really looking forward to how this one unfolds.

comments.author: onions212
comments.body: More footmen frenzy can't be a bad thing

comments.author: Nebin_Terrick
comments.body: Only hero styled game I've played like this is a little league. Will be interesting to control and army while you have a hero. Only can hope we get a goblin faction.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body:
I'm somewhat jealous of people who are recently laid off. Gives you an abundance of time to focus on the game alongside family and health. For me I've been grinding work then come home to grind my game. Hardly any time left for other things. 

Sure I could easily quit my job but then that means losing a steady, predictable flow of income.

replies.author: SoberSonderr
replies.body:
Well, if it makes you feel any better, the lead up for the layoff was extremely stressful. To be completely honest, one of the main reasons I have been able to do this is because of my wife's support and encouragement to keep this up and not give up. 

It's been increasingly difficult with the sentiment surrounding AI on reddit as well. Most people's perception is that I just type in "hey make my game" and suddenly my game is made. What people don't know is the game design, the bug fixing, testing, server infrastructure, architecture, history, triggers, sounds, pretty much everything else being involved with it. 

I also want to mention I had a nice rainy day fund saved up to support something like this. Admittedly, the stable income has been sorely missed.

comments.author: 12Kwedge
comments.body: FINALLY! I've been talking to my friend about a footies remake since DOTA2 came out.  The game looks pretty good so far for a solo dev. I can't wait to try the demo in January. Wishlisted on steam :)
